item.title: Its Lonely At The Bottom
item.description:
“Never be wrong on your own”

John Maynard Keynes

Except of course that he probably never said it, or if he did it was not recorded as a direct quote. What he did say was below. The motto of Bankers everywhere. We should not be churlish about this, its good advice. In theory the odds of a colossal mistake should diminish with the more eyes looking at the problem. Eventually someone who knows what they are doing should figure out the problem. The challenge here is group think, where the bias rules the day.

item.title: Hard Power
item.description:
“Before you step out of that circle give me a reply to lay before the senate” - Gaius Popillius Laenas, Consul of Rome

Roman consul, Gaius Popillius Laenas drew the veritable line in the sand. That line being a circle. It was circa 168 BCE, and Antiochus IV Epiphanes was advancing on Alexandria, threatening to conquer Egypt. Rome was not impressed. One single man, with a small retinue, standing in front of an entire army, delivered quite the message. Antiochus IV pondered, and caved to the credible threat of Rome. He placed in his hand the Roman decree, or senatus-consultum ordering him to put an end at once to the war with Ptolemy, before stating the ultimatum as above. Source: Polybius, Greek historian. He was a contemporary of the time.

item.title: Power Absolute
item.description: “I cannot accept your canon that we are to judge Pope and King unlike other men, with a favourable presumption that they did no wrong. If there is any presumption it is the other way against holders of power, increasing as the power increases. Historic responsibility has to make up for the want of legal responsibility. Power tends to corrupt and absolute power corrupts absolutely. Great men are almost always bad men, even when they exercise influence and not authority: still more when you superadd the tendency or the certainty of corruption by authority. There is no worse heresy than that the office sanctifies the holder of it. That is the point at which the negation of Catholicism and the negation of Liberalism meet and keep high festival, and the end learns to justify the means. You would hang a man of no position, like Ravaillac; but if what one hears is true, then Elizabeth asked the gaoler to murder Mary, and William III ordered his Scots minister to extirpate a clan. Here are the greater names coupled with the greater crimes. You would spare these criminals, for some mysterious reason. I would hang them, higher than Haman, for reasons of quite obvious justice; still more, still higher, for the sake of historical science.” - John Emerich Edward Dalberg, aka Lord Acton.

item.title: Its A You Problem
item.description:
“In the British Army, there are no good battalions and no bad battalions, no good regiments and no bad regiments. There are only good and bad officers.” - General Slim. Defeat into Victory is an account of the retaking of Burma by Allied forces during the Second World War by the British Field Marshal William Slim.

This is the same as the Napoleon quote of “No poor soldiers, only poor officers”, which is the same concept of only poor workers blame their tools. The wider extrapolation here is that if it goes wrong, you have to own it. It is, quite literally, a ‘you’ problem. Even if the staff are incompetent, it can only be so because you tolerated incompetence or you hired the incompetent.

item.title: Approxmimately Right

In chapter 22 the author writes: “It is better to be vaguely right than exactly wrong” (Read, 1898, p. 351). It’s there, I checked. I can also spell (mostly), the title is to make the point. https://www.gutenberg.org/files/18440/18440-h/18440-h.htm

item.title: The Rise Of The Machine
item.description: You are only what the system says you are. Beware the rise of the machine. I write this reading an article on a UK born and bred midwife, facing immigration expulsion from Canada on grounds of a technical problem with the confirmation of her English language test. Yes, this is insane. Doubly so for forcing her to take the test in the first place. When no sane person within the system argues against blindly following “the rules”, we are all doomed. “We are sorry you are dissatisfied with our service today, the system says you are scheduled for Euthanasia. Your complaint is now set to ‘resolved’. Please enjoy your day.”

item.title: About
item.description:
This is a personal site. The writing here covers economics, data analytics, computer science, credit risk, philosophy, and whatever else earns a place. The posts are notes made public — working through ideas, not finished arguments.

The day job

Finance. Primarily credit — analysis, structure, the forensics of how things fail. If you have spent time reading financial statements with genuine scepticism rather than confirmation bias, you will find some common ground here.
